speaker: NARRATOR
text: [storyteller, lighter] San Francisco, the 1950s. Two heart doctors, Meyer Friedman and Ray Rosenman, have a waiting-room problem.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [casual] Their chairs need fixing. So they call in an upholsterer.

speaker: UPHOLSTERER
text: [looking the chairs over, puzzled] Huh. [beat] What kinda patients you got in here, doc?

speaker: FRIEDMAN
text: [busy, clipped, not looking up] Heart patients. Why?

speaker: UPHOLSTERER
text: [matter-of-fact, tapping the chair] 'Cause they only wear out the FRONT of the seat. Look. Nobody in here ever sits back.

speaker: YOU
text: [small laugh] That's me in every waiting room.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [amused, then slowing] Nobody sat back. They perched. Right on the edge. Ready to spring up.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [thoughtful, building] As Friedman later told the story, that was the moment it clicked. Maybe the people getting heart disease had something in common.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: Always on the edge of the seat.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [playful] They gave it a name you've definitely heard.

speaker: NARRATOR
text: [slower, with a hint of doubt] And for a while, it looked like a breakthrough.
